summary.name: OnyX
summary.one_liner: OnyX is a free multifunction maintenance utility for Mac that checks system files, cleans caches, runs maintenance tasks, uninstalls apps, and exposes hidden Apple application settings.
use_cases: Clearing caches and temporary files on a Mac
Verifying the startup disk and system file structure
Changing hidden Finder, Dock, Safari, or Apple app settings
Running a version of OnyX matched to an older macOS release
summary.what_it_does: OnyX verifies the structure of system files and the startup disk. It performs cleaning and maintenance tasks, deletes caches, and removes certain problematic files and folders. It can rebuild various databases and indexes and uninstall applications. It also configures parameters in the Finder, Dock, Safari, and some Apple applications, giving a graphical interface to tasks that otherwise need command-line commands. Separate builds are published for each major macOS release, from current versions back to Mac OS X 10.2.
notable: Separate OnyX version for each major macOS release, from Mac OS X 10.2 to macOS Golden Gate 27
Provides a GUI for tasks that normally need Terminal commands
Listed in awesome-mac under System Related Tools as freeware
caveats: Must use the version matching your macOS release; older versions are not meant for newer systems
Old versions (for macOS Tahoe and earlier) are discontinued and will no longer be updated
Some legacy versions (Mac OS X 10.5 and earlier) only open from an administrator account and require PowerPC or Intel hardware
